chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ribat, who linked it up (to the Imam), saying:

A man complained to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) about his needs, so he said to him: 'Know that whatever you acquire from this world beyond your sustenance, you are merely a treasurer for others in it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on surplus wealth beyond one's basic needs?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (AS) defines the ethical boundary of personal wealth, teaching that any provision exceeding one's necessary sustenance (*qut*) is held in trust (*amanah*) for the broader community. This concept underscores the Shia understanding of economic justice, where surplus is not merely charity but a divine stewardship, linking individual accumulation to communal welfare and the rights of the poor.
